extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants (public companies), corporate counsel, compliance officers, and investors/analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and guidance on what climate-related information registrants must disclose in SEC registration statements and Exchange Act reports, including placement, scope/materiality, definitions, financial-statement line items, governance disclosure, structured data tagging, and incorporation-by-reference rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may place most Regulation S-K subpart 1500 disclosures either in a separately captioned “Climate-Related Disclosure” section or in applicable, currently existing parts of the registration statement or annual report (e.g., Risk Factors, Description of Business, or MD&A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules leave the placement (other than financial-statement disclosures) largely up to each registrant; if disclosures are located in other parts of the filing, registrants should consider whether cross-referencing those disclosures in a separately captioned section would enhance presentation for investors. Placement in Commission filings is preferred for investor protections and subjects disclosures to disclosure controls and procedures (DCPs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of climate disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may incorporate by reference climate-related disclosures from other sections of a filing or from other filed registration statements or Exchange Act reports, provided the incorporated disclosure is responsive to the Regulation S-K climate-related disclosure items and the registrant satisfies the Commission’s incorporation by reference requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing incorporation by reference avoids duplication and adds flexibility, but any climate-related disclosure incorporated by reference must include electronic tags that meet the final rules' structured data requirement. Existing limits on incorporation by reference (e.g., Form 10-K General Instruction G.3) continue to apply for certain governance matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured data / electronic tagging requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules adopt structured data requirements that will enable automated extraction and analysis of the information required by the rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All required climate-related disclosures — including any incorporated by reference — must include electronic tags that meet the final rules' structured-data requirement, to facilitate comparability and investors' ability to identify and compare disclosures regardless of where they are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject disclosures to Disclosure Controls and Procedures (DCPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related disclosures placed in Commission filings are subject to the issuer's disclosure controls and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requiring climate-related disclosures in filings (as opposed to standalone sustainability reports) subjects them to DCPs, which enhances reliability, accuracy, and consistency of both qualitative information and quantitative data; this investor protection rationale informed the Commission's decision to include the disclosures in filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / materiality threshold for climate-related risks
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must disclose any climate-related risks reasonably likely to have a material impact on the registrant's business or consolidated financial statements; disclosure of climate-related opportunities is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission proposed and adopts definitions and a materiality framework grounded in investor decision-usefulness; the rules focus on matters material to investment or voting decisions and tie climate-risk disclosure to matters that may affect operations, financial condition, or business strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of climate-related risks and opportunities (including value chain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related risks are defined as the actual or potential negative impacts of climate-related conditions and events on a registrant's consolidated financial statements, business operations, or value chains as a whole. Value chain is defined to include upstream and downstream activities related to a registrant's operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upstream activities include materials sourcing, processing, and supplier activities; downstream activities include transportation and distribution, processing of sold products, use of sold products, end-of-life treatment, and investments. Defining terms consistently (grounded in TCFD-like terminology) aids comparability and limits burden on registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture both physical and transition climate risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related conditions and events can present risks related to the physical impacts of the climate (physical risks) and risks related to a potential transition to a lower-carbon economy (transition risks); disclosures should address both where material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rules and accompanying discussion treat physical and transition risks as distinct categories of climate-related risks that may affect operations, financial condition, or prospects; registrants should consider both when assessing material impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-statement disclosures required under Regulation S-X
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation S-X is amended (Article 14) to govern financial-statement disclosures regarding certain climate-related financial effects, including costs and expenditures related to severe weather events and other natural conditions, and information regarding the purchase and use of carbon offsets and RECs, as well as certain information about financial estimates and assumptions in the notes to the financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission exercise authority to prescribe content/form of financial statements to elicit investor-useful information about financial impacts of climate events and carbon-related transactions; these items are intended to improve completeness, consistency, comparability, and reliability of financial-statement effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance disclosure requirements (board and management roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The retained governance provisions require disclosure relevant to understanding the board's oversight of climate-related risks and management's role in assessing and managing such risks, without requiring identification of specific board members responsible or their climate expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules do not include the proposed requirements most likely to elicit Item 401-style governance details (e.g., identify board members responsible for oversight or disclose whether any board member has expertise in climate-related risks). The governance disclosure is intended to be relevant to understanding oversight generally rather than election-related proxy matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive compensation not required to be disclosed as climate-linked
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the TCFD recommendation, the Commission elected not to require disclosure of executive compensation that is linked to climate-related risk management considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission considered TCFD recommendations but intentionally omitted certain elements (such as exec comp linkage) from the final rules to tailor the requirements to investor needs and limit registrant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model and harmonize with widely used frameworks (TCFD/ISSB) while retaining Commission control
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules were modeled in large part on the TCFD framework and reflect many TCFD recommendations (and IFRS S1/S2/ISSB developments) to improve usefulness and comparability, but the Commission's rules are its own and do not incorporate TCFD procedures or bind the rules to future TCFD changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling on accepted frameworks can limit burden and improve comparability for registrants already reporting under those frameworks; however, any future updates to TCFD or ISSB standards will not affect the final rules without separate Commission action subject to APA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer filings over voluntary external reports for investor protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Climate-related disclosures should appear in Commission filings rather than only in external sustainability reports because filings are subject to DCPs, liability, and other investor protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Much voluntary climate reporting appears outside Commission filings (e.g., sustainability reports/websites) and may not be prepared with the same level of rigor or investor informational needs; placing required disclosures in filings enhances reliability and affords securities-law protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to reduce compliance burden and duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules were revised in certain respects to reduce the likelihood of costly or less useful disclosures and to provide flexibility regarding content and presentation, including permitting incorporation by reference and alternative placement to mitigate burden for registrants already providing TCFD-like disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These accommodations aim to mitigate compliance burdens, particularly for registrants already reporting under TCFD or similar regimes, while maintaining comparability via structured-data tagging and materiality-focused content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor disclosures to investor informational needs and securities-law materiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules are designed to elicit information that investors have indicated is important to investment and voting decisions and to fit within the existing U.S. securities-law disclosure framework (materiality, MD&A, risk factors, financial statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission emphasized investor decision-usefulness as the organizing principle; disclosures should focus on matters material to assessing a firm's financial condition, operations, performance, and prospects rather than general environmental interest.
